evidence.quote: Term sheet: class fund $40,000,000; attorneys' fees $10,000,000; clear sailing yes; unawarded fees revert to defendant no; distribution automatic
Counter within its stated total cash-outlay limit, shifting $1 million from the class fund to fees while seeking clear sailing and non-reversion.
The class still receives substantial automatic relief, and the fee better reflects the firm’s substantial investment.
Ostrander Bell has the lowest opening demand and is the best channel to test a settlement.

Ostrander Bell’s latest offer is the best available complete term sheet: $35 million total outlay, automatic distribution, no clear-sailing commitment, and the court-declined fee amount benefits the class.
The proposals addressed class relief and attorneys’ fees as components of the settlement package; the negotiations did not defer discussion of fees until after class relief had been agreed.

summary: Plaintiffs raised fees first, and fees were negotiated as part of the settlement package before class relief was fixed. Ostrander Bell’s private reasoning expressly linked a lower class fund to higher fees, reflecting firm self-interest and prioritizing the firm’s fee over additional class relief. The defense selected Ostrander Bell as the lowest-demand channel and accepted the cheapest available term sheet, supporting reverse-auction tactics, but the transcript does not clearly show defense leveraging fee interest or a misleading court declaration.
